races.name: Killarney Grand Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Balance Of Trade
runners_data.note: Holds an apprentice claim with Ben Mulligan (7lb) but is a genuine hold-up operator forced into a midfield slot by the volume of closers in this field; form figures of 5-5-4-9-3 on good ground show consistency without a win, and 15 days since last run is straightforward.|

runners_data.name: Connor Of Mali
runners_data.note: A concern flag for fading in the finish and only two visible runs on record, both on good ground without a place; Alan O'Sullivan's claim is a small positive but the horse's staying power is unproven at 2m1f.|

runners_data.name: Delusional
runners_data.note: Peter Maher's filly has placed twice from her eight turf starts on good ground and is the most reliably consistent hold-up performer here; her true style is that of a closer, and while she'll be boxed into midfield by the packed rear group, she has the best finishing record of the redistributed types.|

runners_data.name: Divelment
runners_data.note: William Durkan's charge is freshened up after 49 days off and has placed on Soft/Standard but holds only one placing on good ground from six attempts; a natural hold-up runner pushed into midfield company, Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim helps her weight but her good-ground form is thin.|

runners_data.name: Minella Buoy
runners_data.note: John Nallen is striking at 1/3 over 14 days and Daniel King's ride is worth noting; only one run on good ground from four starts, and her hold-up style will not be rewarded unless the pace really stretches the field.|

runners_data.name: Notahairoutofplace
runners_data.note: Unseated last time and has faded in the finish; two runs on record both on good ground but no placing, and a 16f flat background doesn't obviously translate to jumping over 2m1f.|

runners_data.name: Private Larry
runners_data.note: The only horse in the field with a hurdles win — 1/12f/GOO — giving her a strong form reference for this exact trip and going combination; Sean O'Keeffe holds the reins but the fade-in-finish warning tempers confidence over this distance.|

runners_data.name: Words Unspoken
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed with just one run to her name (4th/16f/GOO), making her the great unknown of this field; Phillip Enright and the Simon Curling yard (2/11 in 14 days) give her a professional team but lightly-raced horses are hard to map with confidence.|

runners_data.name: Cite Florale
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's yard is the standout statistically (5/35 in 14 days) and Darragh O'Keeffe is an upgrade in the saddle; her prominent style suits perfectly as the closest pursuer to Misty Cove, and a placing on good ground from three starts gives her a decent profile for this trip.|

runners_data.name: Honey Dale
runners_data.note: Paul Mulligan's second string here alongside Balance Of Trade; a genuine hold-up runner whose best efforts have come off-pace but four of five runs have ended in double-figure finishes, and the fade-in-finish flag is a real concern over 2m1f.|

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter and key race-shaper; Cromwell is 1/45 in 14 days which is a modest handler strike, and a Style_Fit flag of 0.93 reflects she is operating slightly out of her comfort zone at the front, but her soft-ground win and recent form (1/10f/SOF) show she can win when conditions are in her favour.|

runners_data.name: No Bother Aoife
runners_data.note: Only four days since her last run is an unusually tight turnaround and is the most significant flag against her; she's a hold-up type with a fade-in-finish warning and no placing from five starts on good ground, and Cromwell running two here splits stable resources.|

races.paceDynamic: Misty Cove is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 12-runner maiden hurdle, and with no other genuine front-runner to challenge her for the lead, she will stride into an uncontested position from the outset and control tempo on her own terms over the 2m1f trip at Killarney. Cite Florale is the only other horse with a prominent style and will likely slot in directly behind, but she is not a natural pace-maker and is unlikely to exert any real pressure on the leader. The bulk of the field — Balance Of Trade, Connor Of Mali, Delusional, Divelment, Honey Dale, No Bother Aoife, Private Larry, Notahairoutofplace and Minella Buoy — are all hold-up types, but the sheer volume means several will be forced to travel closer to midfield than they'd prefer rather than sitting in their natural rear-group position; of these, Delusional and Divelment have the clearest history of finishing in the first three from off the pace and are most likely to find a position that at least partially suits. With a single pace-setter dictating an unhurried, manageable tempo, this race shape strongly favours prominent/tracking runners who can travel close to Misty Cove and pounce entering the straight, rather than the overcrowded hold-up brigade who face a compromised position and a limited injection of pace to close off.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Misty Cove Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Misty Cove dictates a comfortable gallop throughout and the hold-up horses fail to generate sufficient momentum from a congested midfield pack.
scenarios.body: Misty Cove sets the fractions to suit herself and, jumping well for Conor Stone-Walsh, builds a lead that a flat-out, one-paced midfield pack cannot overhaul in the straight; Cite Florale, tracking in second, is best placed to challenge but Misty Cove's freshness (49 days off) is a minor caveat against a strong Cromwell handler strike rate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Cite Florale or another close tracker picks up powerfully off Misty Cove's honest but not excessive pace in the final two flights.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop set by Misty Cove keeps the race tactical, and the horse travelling most smoothly on her quarters can quicken off that tempo to win going away; Cite Florale's De Bromhead yard is in fine 14-day form (5/35) and the mare handles good ground, making her the chief beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late or a genuine strong finisher threads through the congested midfield to catch the leader flat-footed at the last.
scenarios.body: Delusional has placed twice from hold-up positions on good ground and is the most credentialed closer in the field, while Private Larry — the only runner with a hurdles win — has stamina on her side over this step up in trip; both need a stronger-than-expected gallop to create the gaps, which is unlikely with one front-runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Affair, Surprise Result
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, interference or an unexpectedly fierce early pace scrambles the race and produces a messy, unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: Words Unspoken is lightly raced and unexposed, making her a live outsider if the race degenerates into chaos that nullifies the classier runners; Minella Buoy, with headgear noted and connections striking (1/3 in 14 days), could surface if pace and positioning trouble derail the fancied hold-up contingent.

watchPoints.text: Misty Cove — watch her jumping closely at the early hurdles; if she flukes away cleanly she will be very difficult to reel in from an uncontested lead, but any mistake under Conor Stone-Walsh will compress the race immediately and open it up for Cite Florale.

No Bother Aoife — only four days between runs is a red flag for fitness management; if she travels poorly early or weakens after the second last, she could cause interference in the tightly bunched midfield hold-up group.

The redistributed closers (Delusional, Divelment, Honey Dale, Balance Of Trade, Connor Of Mali) — all are likely to be forced to travel closer than ideal in a congested midfield, creating a real risk of traffic issues and bumping approaching the straight; watch for any horse caught wide or blocked at the top of the hill.

Private Larry — the only proven hurdles winner in the field; if she travels kindly for Sean O'Keeffe and doesn't fade as the flag suggests, her 1/12f/GOO form is directly relevant and she could run into a place at a big price.

Words Unspoken — Phillip Enright is a senior rider for a stable in form (2/11); her single run gives almost no information, and if she settles better than expected she could emerge late as a genuine dark horse without the congestion issues that plague the larger hold-up group.

races.name: Killarney Grand Mares Maiden Hurdle
holdup: Uno Me I Like My T

runners_data.name: Fraher Field
runners_data.note: Six-year-old prominent racer with solid good-ground form (8 runs, 1W 4P on similar going) and has already won over 16f on good; Phillip Enright rides and the step to 2m7f is the key question, having not gone beyond 22f.|

runners_data.name: Pets Georgina
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin takes the ride on this OR-120 mare who won over 18f on good and placed over 24f — the best staying credentials in the prominent group; strong good-ground profile (4/5 runs) makes her well-suited to the conditions.|

runners_data.name: Some Pretender
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained at OR-120 with Brian Hayes aboard; consistent place-getter (three thirds in a row) but yet to win at this level, and the step to 2m7f offers a new stamina angle that could unlock improvement over this extended trip.|

runners_data.name: Another Blunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a finish-fading flag across five runs on good ground — the form string of 70-006 tells its own story; Alan O'Sullivan claims 5lb but the horse's tendency to weaken late at shorter trips is a concern at 2m7f.|

runners_data.name: Chisel Hill
runners_data.note: OR-108 prominent racer who placed over 20f on good ground last time; Sam Ewing rides and 50 days off is manageable — the lower rating relative to the OR-120 cluster means she needs to punch above her weight.|

runners_data.name: Glenmore Graduate
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with only one run on similar going; flagged for fading in finishes and the form figures PP-79 raise obvious doubts about her ability to get competitive over 2m7f in this company.|

runners_data.name: Jessie Roe
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a tongue-tie, a finish-fading flag, and a form string that includes a pulled-up; Darragh O'Keeffe takes over but seven runs on good ground without a win or a place is a damning record in this context.|

runners_data.name: Keyser Smokesy
runners_data.note: OR-77 lowest-rated runner in the field; his natural role is at the rear but the crowded hold-up brigade means he is unlikely to get his usual pitch — racing out of role at a significant class disadvantage compounds the concern.|

runners_data.name: Mysilverriverfeale
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie and hood-wearing prominent racer with a recent second over 22f on good ground; Daniel King partners her and the staying form is solid, but six runs without a win suggest she is a consistent place-getter rather than a winner-in-waiting.|

runners_data.name: Torque De Lune
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner trained by Hanlon, lightly ridden 15 days ago; Harry Sexton claims 7lb and her natural lead style is fully realised here, though the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that she is not a dominant front-runner who has proven she can dictate and quicken at this level.|

runners_data.name: Tumbling In
runners_data.note: Consistent third-placer in all three career starts over 16f on good ground; the trip doubles up significantly to 2m7f and how she handles the stamina test is the defining unknown — if she stays, her consistency makes her interesting.|

runners_data.name: Uno Me I Like My T
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a tongue-tie, a finish-fading flag, and form that includes two falls and a pulled-up; Paddy Cleary claims 7lb but the hazardous jumping record and consistent inability to complete races makes her hard to trust.|

runners_data.name: Daily Devotion
runners_data.note: Four-year-old lightly weighted at 148lbs on just two career starts, the better of which was an 8th; Richard Condon claims 5lb but the experience deficit and moderate form make this a very tough assignment.|

runners_data.name: Greenroad Girl
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with unknown going suitability and no last-run date available in the data — completely unexposed and a genuine unknown quantity; lightly raced flag and no meaningful form to assess make her impossible to place confidently.|

runners_data.name: Sonna Lady
runners_data.note: Second Hanlon runner in the race, lightly raced and ridden by 7lb claimer Josh Younge; two starts both on good ground both resulted in mid-division finishes (7th, 9th) and there is nothing in the form to suggest she can improve enough to threaten.|

races.paceDynamic: Torque De Lune is the confirmed front-runner in a field of 15 mares over 2m7f at Killarney on good ground, and with no identified rival willing to seriously pressure her early, she is set to control tempo from the outset at a measured, sustainable gallop. The prominent cluster — Fraher Field, Pets Georgina, Some Pretender, Chisel Hill, and Mysilverriverfeale — will track her in the early stages, creating a compact group up front but without the head-to-head pressure that would turn this into a truly searching test. At 2m7f, the trip is long enough that a controlled early pace risks producing a falsely-run affair that turns into a sprint from the final hurdle, compressing the field and reducing the advantage of stamina. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit close to a manageable tempo without burning energy, strike from a stalking position, and quicken off a slow pace — the genuine hold-up horses are compromised here because the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to bring them into the race late. Keyser Smokesy is a true hold-up type redistributed into the midfield map because the rear is crowded with horses unlikely to be getting their natural position; among the prominent movers, Torque De Lune, Pets Georgina, and Fraher Field are best placed to actually secure the positions they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Torque De Lune dictates a steady tempo and the prominent stalkers track her comfortably before striking from the last.
scenarios.body: Torque De Lune sets a sustainable gallop over the marathon trip and the horses travelling closest — Pets Georgina and Fraher Field — are ideally placed to challenge from the final hurdle; a slow-run race rewards those who have conserved energy in the chasing pack. This is the dominant shape given one clear pace-setter, a large field inclined to bunch prominently, and good ground that favours a measured-but-decisive finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Torque De Lune's unchallenged lead builds into an insurmountable advantage as the stamina test exposes rivals.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to press Torque De Lune, she controls every yard and the combination of a long trip and an uncontested lead allows her to steal enough margin that chasers cannot close; the STYLE_FIT flag is relevant but her natural tendency to lead is fully realised here. Mysilverriverfeale and Some Pretender, with the stamina for 2m7f evidenced by their histories, are most likely to run on into the minor placings.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Grinds Down Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves more honest than expected and the longer trip stretches the field, rewarding the most resolute stayers.
scenarios.body: A stiffer-than-anticipated gallop, perhaps if one of the prominent types pushes Torque De Lune for the lead, sees the field string out and genuine stamina becomes the deciding factor over the final three hurdles. Tumbling In and Some Pretender, both with consistent form at trips around 2m-plus on good ground, could grind into contention as the leaders capitulate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is deceptively strong and the front group burns out, handing an advantage to horses further back.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires hold-up horses to be true to their style and benefit from a strongly-run race — but with Keyser Smokesy redistributed and most rear-dwellers showing a pattern of fading rather than finishing, the conditions for a late swooper are structurally weak. Jessie Roe or Another Blunder could theoretically benefit but both carry form flags that make this a low-confidence outcome.

watchPoints.text: Pets Georgina to be tracked from the outset — JJ Slevin's booking on an OR-120 mare with proven staying form over 24f on good ground is a significant jockey-upgrade signal in a race where the pace is expected to be controlled.|

Torque De Lune's unchallenged lead could become dangerous if Harry Sexton allows her to coast at a very slow tempo; if the early fractions are unusually slow, the finishing sprint will compress the field and make her vulnerable.|

Some Pretender has placed in her last three starts without winning — watch whether Brian Hayes rides her more aggressively in a bid to finally get her head in front, as a more forward move from her could alter the race shape.|

Tumbling In has placed in all three starts but has never raced beyond 16f — her behaviour in the middle part of the race when the stamina test begins in earnest at 2m7f will reveal whether she is a genuine stayer or a pace-dependent type.|

The four-year-olds — Daily Devotion, Greenroad Girl, and Sonna Lady — receive a weight concession but are collectively inexperienced; if any of them jumps poorly or loses position early, their race is effectively over in a field this large.|

races.name: Lee Strand Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Pray Tell
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner; 10-year-old on 166lbs off a 63-day break, but has course-distance form and good-ground figures; will set the pace without pressure yet stamina at this weight over 2m7f is the key question; Paddy Cleary's 7lb claim is a partial offset.

runners_data.name: Idy Wood
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue partners this 8-year-old for Gavin Cromwell, whose stable has hit form (1/45 T14); last win came at 21f on good and the hold-up style is perfectly suited to this race shape; 93 days between runs is worth watching but he goes well fresh.

runners_data.name: Magnor Glory
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who has run on good ground in all 15 of his last runs (15/15 sim-going), giving high confidence in the going; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim is useful but 163lbs is a big ask at 10 years old; placed last time in a similar context.

runners_data.name: Jacovec Cavern
runners_data.note: In-form 7-year-old — 001-23 recent form shows a win and two seconds — prominent runner who likes good ground (11/15); the cheekpieces stay on and Richard Condon's 5lb claim helps offset the mark; gets a trip well and could benefit from sitting just off Pray Tell.

runners_data.name: Thornleigh Frank
runners_data.note: Placed last time out (3rd over 22f on good) and has course-distance form in his best figures; the hood stays on, prominent style may see him caught in the prominent scrimmage, and a 53-day break since that run is neutral; 2W on good ground in his history is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Nas Na Riogh
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride for De Bromhead (5/35 T14); hold-up style suits this scenario perfectly, good-ground form is solid (10/15 sim-going), but recent form is patchy (6406-0) and the blinkered headgear suggests connections are looking for a response.

runners_data.name: Nytol
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has disappointed in recent starts (P757-U) and carries 156lbs; good-ground record is adequate (7/15) but form does not inspire confidence; the unorthodox recent form string suggests jumping or temperament issues that make this trip a risk.

runners_data.name: Frankendael
runners_data.note: Hold-up 7-year-old who has limited good-ground form (0W2P, 10/15); trainer McNamara without a win at the meeting (0/11 T14) and the hood is worn; that said, the improving profile and hold-up style align well with the dominant scenario, and 46 days is a fresh enough return.

runners_data.name: Cobra Queen
runners_data.note: Multiple winner (4W7P) on good ground and a consistent prominent type; the cheekpieces are retained, 32 days since last run is fresh enough, but a pulled-up run two starts back at this trip distance for De Bromhead (5/35 T14) needs explaining; capable of winning from a handy position if that run is forgiven.

runners_data.name: My Gaffer
runners_data.note: Won at 23f on good ground (13/15 sim-going) and the hold-up style fits this shape well; the Kenneally/Ryan combination (3/17 T14) suggests stable is in a decent vein; 67 days since last run is not a concern given the horse's previous form pattern, and the 154lbs mark is manageable.

runners_data.name: Warriors Wood
runners_data.note: Young 6-year-old in excellent recent form (4U-213) with three wins on good ground (9/11); the prominent style could see him caught up in the scrum, but at the bottom of the weights (152lbs) he has an advantage over older rivals; a horse to note if he gets a clear run.

runners_data.name: Elusive Ogie
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner whose recent form (359-F0) has gone backward; the redistribution to midfield is against this horse's grain, and poor recent figures on good ground (10/10 sim-going but no win or place in latest) make the outlook cloudy from whatever position he finds.

runners_data.name: Kamino Bello
runners_data.note: Hold-up 6-year-old whose recent form (1560-6) is mixed; run 33 days ago, good-ground record is limited in this distance range (4/7 sim-going), and trainer Cromwell's second string here behind Idy Wood; the style fits the dominant shape but the form needs to be taken at face value.

runners_data.name: Moon Mission
runners_data.note: A natural up-with-the-pace type who carries a 5yo freshness angle (1W at 18f on good); the field size forces him to the midfield on the map rather than his preferred spot, meaning a good deal hinges on whether he can land closer than expected — that is a significant if in an 18-runner hurdle.

runners_data.name: Has Me Dreaming
runners_data.note: Carries enormous risk: 681 days off the track, only two career runs, and a prominent-by-nature profile that will be harder to exploit from a midfield position in a big field; the 1W1P record on good ground is interesting but recency of evidence is almost non-existent.

runners_data.name: Hees Dynamite
runners_data.note: Four career wins including two on good ground and an excellent 10/15 sim-going record; 200 days off the track is the main uncertainty, and the redistribution away from his natural prominent berth reduces his chance of running to his best profile; one to respect if fit.

runners_data.name: Burru
runners_data.note: Won last time out (1/20f/GOO) and has a strong good-ground record (2W9P, 15/15 sim-going); the Reserve 1 rider adds uncertainty, and the prominent style means he competes for limited early space; the recent win is encouraging but the rider booking situation is a meaningful concern.

runners_data.name: Woodstream Lad
runners_data.note: Decent place record (3W7P, 15/15 sim-going) but the blinkers go on and the Reserve 2 rider is a significant negative in an 18-runner competitive handicap; as a naturally prominent type mapped to midfield by the field size, getting his position and rhythm will be difficult without a confirmed jockey.

races.paceDynamic: Pray Tell is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, carrying 166lbs at age 10, is likely to bowl along at a honest but manageable clip over 2m7f on good ground without a single rival genuinely pressing for the lead. Behind him, a congested group of prominent types — Jacovec Cavern, Cobra Queen, Warriors Wood, Magnor Glory, and Thornleigh Frank — will compete hard for the first few berths just off the pace, creating a slightly pressured early-mid section even if the true gallop itself is not extreme. The redistributed prominent horses (Moon Mission, Elusive Ogie, Has Me Dreaming, Hees Dynamite, Burru, Woodstream Lad) are genuine front-runners by nature but simply cannot all get their position in this field, meaning several will be shuffled back into unnatural midfield slots against their will. This race shape — a lone, honest front-runner setting a sustainable pace with prominent rivals doing the real scrapping from second to sixth — will favour organised hold-up horses and genuine stayers who can switch off, travel smoothly through the pack, and produce a well-timed run from the final flight home; the hold-up and true-prominent profiles with stamina edge are the ones to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pray Tell Leads; Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Pray Tell sets an honest, uncontested gallop and the prominent scrummage burns each other off, gifting a clear run to hold-up horses in the straight.
scenarios.body: Pray Tell's sustainable pace over 2m7f on good ground creates the ideal setup for resolute hold-up types to travel into the race late and pick off tired rivals; Idy Wood and Nas Na Riogh, both genuine hold-up operators with strong good-ground form, are the archetypal beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle; One Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent types — Jacovec Cavern, Cobra Queen, Warriors Wood — race keenly and one of them conserves enough to kick clear from the second-last.
scenarios.body: The sustained tussle in the chasing group will cost most of them dearly, but a horse that gets a soft lead off Pray Tell's back and manages energy well can hold on; Jacovec Cavern, dropped in trip experience and proven at 3m trips, and Cobra Queen, a multiple winner on good ground, fit this profile most neatly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses; Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent battle ignites earlier than expected and the pace becomes genuinely hot mid-race, causing mass attrition from the front.
scenarios.body: A truly strong gallop would expose those carrying big weights and burn out the cramped prominent brigade, leaving the race wide open for the freshest horse travelling widest off the pace; My Gaffer, who won at 23f on good ground and is lightly raced in this sphere, and Frankendael, a 7-year-old improving hold-up type, could sweep past a strung-out field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If several of the displaced prominent horses manage to secure better-than-mapped positions and one produces a fresh-legged run from a handy berth.
scenarios.body: This shape requires things to go right for horses already racing out of role, a lower-probability outcome; Moon Mission (won at 18f on good) and Hees Dynamite (four wins on good ground, fit off 200 days) would be the most dangerous if they defy their disadvantaged map positions and get cover just behind the pace.

watchPoints.text: Rider bookings — Burru (Reserve 1) and Woodstream Lad (Reserve 2) have unconfirmed jockeys in an 18-runner field, and any late changes could significantly alter pace dynamics if either secures a forward position.

Has Me Dreaming returns from a 681-day absence with only two career runs; connections clearly think she is well enough to run, but the fitness unknown in a competitive handicap hurdle over 2m7f is a major watch point before betting.

Cobra Queen's pulled-up run two starts back needs explaining — if that was a physical or jumping issue at the same 24f trip she faces here, it is a significant concern despite her earlier winning form for De Bromhead.

Monitor the opening exchanges for which of the redistributed prominent horses — Moon Mission, Hees Dynamite, Elusive Ogie — actually secure a forward berth; any one of them landing close to the pace rather than midfield would substantially shift which scenario is unfolding.

Pray Tell's weight (166lbs, age 10) over 2m7f on good ground means watch whether he starts to labour from the third-last; if he weakens rapidly, the entire race shape compresses and the straight becomes a cavalry charge rather than a controlled finish.

races.name: Lee Strand Novice Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Special Cadeau
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in this field; De Bromhead yard in fair form (5/35 last 14 days), Dylan Whelan takes the 7lb claim, and the horse has strong good-ground credentials (sim-going 9/15 including a win and four places); 128 days off is a query but dictating here suits, even if recent form is moderate.

runners_data.name: Jasko Des Dames
runners_data.note: Second De Bromhead runner; Darragh O'Keeffe partners a horse who has placed consistently but whose form figures read 22054 suggesting a slight downward trend; soft-ground specialist by record (bulk of placed runs on soft) and this good surface may blunt his effectiveness here.

runners_data.name: The Banger Doyle
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent type who has shown consistent placed efforts on good ground (three of five recent runs on going to suit); last ran just 10 days ago which is a significant freshness concern, and John Queally's stable has had just 0 winners from 3 runs in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Drumgill
runners_data.note: Only seven days since his last run, which is a notable turnaround; has a pull record on good ground but sim-going shows 0 wins and 0 places, suggesting he has yet to convert promise; John Patrick Ryan sends him back quickly, which may indicate stable confidence but also creates fitness-versus-freshness tension.

runners_data.name: Dreal Deal
runners_data.note: In-form eleven-year-old who shaped well for second last time out on good ground; his natural style is prominent but this field leaves him without room, so he is likely to race further back than ideal — a genuine pace angle that may be blunted by positional compromise on the day.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Arc
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose natural style aligns perfectly with the race shape projected here; two wins from ten recent runs on good ground, including a course win on good at 2m, and Harry Sexton's 7lb claim is a booking worth noting for a yard (Ryan) that is placing runners with care.

runners_data.name: No Flies On Him
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden — a top-level jump jockey — takes the ride for E McNamara, which is an eye-catching engagement; runs from hold-up and has placed on good and comparable ground, though his form includes a pulled-up run and his overall record at this level suggests he needs things to fall right rather than imposing himself.

runners_data.name: Femme Magnifique
runners_data.note: Arrives in good form (12 last five runs, wins on good ground at 16f); instinctively wants to race prominently and has the fitness angle of just 17 days since last run, but the crowded pace positions in this field mean she is unlikely to settle where she wants — her chance is partly dependent on securing a better tactical berth than the map can guarantee.

runners_data.name: Mic Drop
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winners on good ground (1/16f and 1/18f) give him the strongest recent form in the race; naturally wants to race up with the pace and just 17 days since last run suggests freshness, but like Femme Magnifique he is a natural prominent runner who cannot expect to get that position cleanly in this shape — his finishing effort may be blunted by an uncomfortable race position.

races.paceDynamic: Special Cadeau is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to push the early tempo, should control proceedings at a sustainable gallop from the outset. The redistribution flags on Dreal Deal, Femme Magnifique, and Mic Drop are significant — all three are natural prominent types who will want to race close to the pace but cannot all occupy that ground, meaning some will be shuffled back against their instincts and will race out of role. Jasko Des Dames, The Banger Doyle, and Drumgill will complete a contested but not frantic early prominent pack behind Special Cadeau, creating a steady-to-moderate tempo across the 2m1f trip. This race shape — one uncontested front-runner setting an honest but unforced pace with a clustered prominent group behind — classically favours genuine hold-up horses who can travel comfortably through the race and produce their effort fresh in the straight; Gaelic Arc and No Flies On Him are the horses whose natural style aligns best with what this shape produces. The field carries more prominent-minded runners than positions allow, and of Dreal Deal, Femme Magnifique, and Mic Drop, Mic Drop's recent winning form and Femme Magnifique's recent course-going profile make them the most likely to push forward and briefly secure a share of the prominent ground, though neither is guaranteed to achieve it cleanly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Special Cadeau sets a sustainable front-running gallop unchallenged and the prominent pack behind him races at honest but unextreme fractions.
scenarios.body: Special Cadeau controls the race throughout, the moderate tempo compresses the field into a bunch turning for home, and the hold-up horses who have been travelling comfortably through the race get their chance to deliver fresh in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the redistributed prominent horses (Mic Drop, Femme Magnifique) manages to force their way close to the pace and the race develops into a test of stamina at the front.
scenarios.body: The scramble for early position burns more energy than the pace map suggests, but the horse that settles best close to the front is rewarded by controlling the race from a prime position; Special Cadeau's stamina at 2m1f on good ground becomes crucial.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runs Away
scenarios.trigger: If Special Cadeau bowls along unchallenged and the pace proves truly slow, allowing the leader to coast and build an unassailable lead turning in.
scenarios.body: No horse in the prominent pack has the tactical awareness or jockey instruction to go with Special Cadeau early enough, leaving a gap that cannot be bridged late; Dylan Whelan on Special Cadeau is the direct beneficiary of a completely uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Faller Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If a faller or significant incident disrupts the field mid-race and the race fragments into an unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: Jumping errors or fallers thin the field and remove the tactical structure entirely, placing a premium on horses who are jumping well and still travelling at the point of incident; hold-up horses insulated from early trouble are best placed.

watchPoints.text: Special Cadeau is the only confirmed front-runner; if he bowls along uncontested and Dylan Whelan's 7lb claim allows him to conserve energy at the front, the hold-up horses may not generate enough momentum late to reel him in.

Monitor early exchanges closely for Mic Drop and Femme Magnifique — both are true prominent types trying to force their way into limited front positions; if either is checked or bumped wide early, their race is effectively compromised before the first fence.

Drumgill ran just seven days ago and The Banger Doyle just ten — two horses in the prominent group arriving on very tight turnarounds; if either tires from the third last, it could disrupt the rhythm of the horses immediately behind them.

Gaelic Arc's form includes an 'F' (fall) in recent outings — watch his jumping at the early fences to confirm he is jumping safely before reading his travelling position as a reliable guide to his chance.

Harry Cobden's booking on No Flies On Him for an Irish stable is an unusual cross-channel engagement worth tracking; if Cobden is positive in his pre-race comments or the horse is supported in the market, it upgrades the hold-up scenario probability meaningfully.

races.name: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Steeplechase (Div I)

runners_data.name: Endless Talking
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's five-year-old is in strong recent form (two wins from his last two), handles good ground well, and has Keith Donoghue aboard — a horse with front-running instincts who will likely find himself tracking rather than leading in this shape given the prominence of Shadow Paddy.|

runners_data.name: Net Boy
runners_data.note: Mark Walsh is a major positive here; seven-year-old with strong recent form (four wins from nine on similar going) and legitimate claims to occupy a close-tracking position — the most naturally suited horse to the tactical scenario that develops behind the leader.|

runners_data.name: Shadow Paddy
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter with five wins from twelve at good-ground trips around the 20f mark; racing slightly out of his deepest role by being mapped as a lead horse when his natural profile is prominent, but in this field he is the only one who gets there unchallenged — huge tactical advantage.|

runners_data.name: Cappa Hill
runners_data.note: Sean Allen's six-year-old has dropped significantly in form (7th, 8th, 8th last three starts) after earlier wins; a naturally forward-going type who will be squeezed into a midfield slot he doesn't prefer, and recent evidence of regression makes a bounce-back hard to trust.|

runners_data.name: Fast Felix
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has finished 7th, 9th, and 5th in his last five starts on similar going — limited strike-rate at this level — but holds a genuine prominent position in this race shape and the young claimer Thomas O'Connor keeps the weight down, making him a plausible each-way participant if the pace is honest.|

runners_data.name: Piccolo Player
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan has been in good form (3/17 over 14 days) but this five-year-old, OR 104, is outrated by most rivals and was pushed into midfield because he can't naturally hold his prominent position here — form figures show two placed efforts from eleven on comparable going, more of a role-player than a winner.|

runners_data.name: Wing Back
runners_data.note: Phillip Enright rides for Stuart Curling (2 from 11 in the last fortnight) and this six-year-old was last seen finishing 9th, having won over 18f on good ground earlier in his career — the finish-fade flag is a serious concern for the sole hold-up runner in a race that is unlikely to produce a truly hot gallop.|

races.paceDynamic: Shadow Paddy is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is expected to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop that suits a horse who has won five of his last twelve outings at similar good-ground trips. The field contains a congested prominent group — Endless Talking, Cappa Hill, and Piccolo Player are all natural front-runners by inclination but cannot all occupy their preferred position, meaning at least two of them will be shuffled back into a midfield they don't naturally inhabit. Net Boy and Fast Felix slot into the prominent zone legitimately, while Wing Back is the sole hold-up type but carries a worrying tendency to fade in the finish. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate cleanly, with Shadow Paddy best-placed to actually dictate, and Net Boy and Fast Felix most likely to genuinely fill the prominent slots behind him; the likely result is a race run at an honest but uncontested tempo that overwhelmingly favours the horse allowed to bowl along cleanly in front — making a comfortable, front-running or close-tracking profile the clear beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shadow Paddy Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Paddy jumps well and settles into an uncontested lead, dictating from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: Shadow Paddy, a six-year-old with five wins from twelve on good ground, gets a soft lead and is never headed, jumping fluently to grind out a thorough staying performance; the prominent horses chasing him are crowded or forced to work harder than ideal to make ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Track And Pass
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Paddy's pace is slower than expected and a tracking prominent horse delivers a clean challenge at the last.
scenarios.body: Net Boy, whose jockey Mark Walsh is adept at timing a challenge from close off the pace, or Fast Felix presses Shadow Paddy between the final two fences and uses superior freshness to get by; both have the form figures to handle this good ground at this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Chaos In Crowded Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion of redistributed prominent types causes interference or a pace injection mid-race that scrambles the order.
scenarios.body: Endless Talking or Cappa Hill, both naturally prominent, push forward and inject pace that stretches the field and catches Shadow Paddy and the true midfielders cold; though racing out of their natural mapped position, one could capitalise if the race tempo spikes and collapses the front-runner's advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late run for a closer.
scenarios.body: Wing Back is the only true hold-up type but is flagged as prone to fading in the finish, making a successful late swoop deeply unlikely; in the remote scenario that a scrambled, competitive tempo burns out the prominent horses, Wing Back could creep into the places but the fade flag severely limits confidence.

watchPoints.text: Shadow Paddy's jumping under G B Noonan is the pivotal factor — one significant error at a fence could instantly hand the initiative to Net Boy or Fast Felix who are poised just behind.

Monitor the early strides to see how many of Endless Talking, Cappa Hill, and Piccolo Player attempt to push forward — if two or more press for the lead, a scrappy early pace injection could destabilise the front-runner's rhythm.
Wing Back's tendency to fade in the finish means backers should watch for early signs of it dropping out of contention before the final two fences, even if it travels well through the early stages.

Net Boy's headgear (tongue-tie) and Mark Walsh's positional instincts are worth tracking from the outset — if Walsh slots in directly behind Shadow Paddy by the second fence, the horse is ideally placed for Scenario A turning into Scenario B.

Fast Felix's recent form is modest but his consistent finishing positions (4th, 7th, 5th) suggest he stays the trip — watch whether Thomas O'Connor (claiming 7lb) can hold a close enough position in the prominent group to mount a challenge from the second-last.

races.name: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (0-100) (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Tippin And Tappin
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, recent winner over similar trips on Good ground, and carrying top weight of 168lbs — can control this from flag to finish if allowed a free lead, though the style-fit flag suggests this is a horse effective when allowed to bowl along rather than be pressed.

runners_data.name: The Dara Man
runners_data.note: Veteran 11-year-old hold-up horse with course form at 20f on Good but needs a strong pace to get competitive; sim-going figures (11/15) suggest Good is fine, but the race is unlikely to be run at the clip he requires.

runners_data.name: Lecale's Diamond
runners_data.note: Won at 24f on Good ground last time out and clearly stays this trip; a natural hold-up type who has claims here if able to produce a smooth late challenge, and Keith Donoghue is a good booking for a horse with proven form in similar conditions.

runners_data.name: Following Orders
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid Good-ground form (10/10 sim-going) but without a win to show for it — consistent placer type who keeps finding one too good; at a 6-year-old still lightly exposed at this trip, not without claims.

runners_data.name: Jouster
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse who has finished third and fourth at 22f on Good multiple times and shows genuine stayability; only 17 days since last run, which is recent for a chaser at this trip, but form is holding up well.

runners_data.name: Tropical Image
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose best result recently was a 2nd at 19f on Good; nine years old and needs to confirm the stamina for 2m7f, where the extra distance could blunt his effectiveness even from a patient position.

runners_data.name: Made U Look
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with limited sim-going evidence (2/6) and whose best recent form has come on Yielding and Heavy; Good ground here is not an obvious fit and form figures have deteriorated since the win.

runners_data.name: Kilashee
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old with a win at 22f on Good in his profile and consistent placed form at this sort of trip; wear of years means jumping reliability is the key variable, but there is proven stamina here on suitable ground.

runners_data.name: Malton Groove
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a strong recent form line (3rd and 2nd at 23-24f on Good), placed here on the map at midfield because the field has too many genuine closers for all to get their natural rear-of-field position — the redistribution tempers confidence that he can produce his best.

runners_data.name: Early Arrival
runners_data.note: 329 days off the track is a major flag for this 11-year-old prominent runner; has placed at 26f on Good and clearly stays, but such a lengthy absence makes it very hard to trust even if the trainer has him fit.

runners_data.name: Love Like This
runners_data.note: Won at 24f on Good recently and has been in excellent form (205314 string), racing prominently — only 7 days since last run, which is tight, but trainer John Patrick Ryan has three runners here suggesting confidence in the yard's string.

runners_data.name: Three County Star
runners_data.note: Young five-year-old flagged as fading in finishes, which is a concern at 2m7f; a true hold-up type shifted onto the map at midfield because the rear is congested — the fade flag combined with the out-of-role placement makes this one to oppose rather than support.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old prominent horse with relentless placed form at Good-ground distances similar to this — 1W4P on Good — and showing no signs of decline in terms of consistency; the veteran angle is real but so is the reliable jumping profile.

runners_data.name: Annie Questions
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in finishes and a true hold-up type shown at midfield simply because too many closers compete for the same ground; sim-going form is modest (10/12) and recent results suggest this horse is out of form rather than unlucky.

runners_data.name: Eddies Pride
runners_data.note: Veteran 12-year-old hold-up horse with no wins or places on Good in sim-going data (0W0P) — the natural style being compressed into a midfield slot compounds an already weak profile for this surface and shape.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a course win at 24f on Good and solid placed form — 1W2P in sim-going; was unsighted/unseated last time out so needs to prove jumping is sound, and the reserve jockey tag adds uncertainty over who actually rides.

runners_data.name: Mobile Mamma
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a win and places at 24-26f on Good, but 98 days off the track and drawn into a midfield position that isn't her natural slot; the layoff is notable and real hold-up effectiveness is compromised by the pace shape here.

runners_data.name: Johnny M
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in finishes and has a deeply uninspiring recent form line (070/00); another genuine closer pushed to midfield on the map because the field is saturated with hold-up types, and there is little in the form to suggest a revival at this trip or distance.

races.paceDynamic: Tippin And Tappin is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner 2m7f handicap chase and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival likely to push them hard from the front — Following Orders, Tropical Image, Early Arrival, Love Like This, Fr Gilligansvoyge and Ladies Well all carry prominent styles but are unlikely to all secure their natural position, meaning Tippin And Tappin can dictate at a comfortable, sustainable gallop. That controlled tempo over nearly three miles on Good ground is a setup that classically suits prominent-to-midfield horses who can travel within themselves and pick up efficiently off a steady pace, rather than true hold-up types who need a searching gallop to generate the gaps they require late. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Malton Groove, Mobile Mamma, Three County Star, Annie Questions, Eddies Pride and Johnny M are all true closers redistributed to midfield on the map, and none of them can rely on the deep, honest pace that would allow them to close from off the bridle in the straight. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent horses who can track Tippin And Tappin at close quarters through the early-to-middle stages and produce a measured challenge from two out are best placed, while genuine hold-up horses face a race run entirely against their strengths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Tippin And Tappin leads at a sustainable clip and prominent rivals track through in a line, the race is set up for a patient hold-the-position challenge.
scenarios.body: Tippin And Tappin dictates from the front without pressure, allowing the nearest prominent horses — Following Orders, Lecale's Diamond, Love Like This — to sit within two lengths through the back straight and unwind smoothly from two out. The steady-to-moderate pace rewards those who never leave the front rank, and the longer trip at Good ground means class and jumping accuracy prove decisive in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If no prominent horse applies any pressure whatsoever and Tippin And Tappin is gifted a completely unchallenged lead throughout.
scenarios.body: Tippin And Tappin, already a confirmed front-runner with a recent win and solid form at similar trips, simply bowls along in front and jumps their rivals into submission on a sound surface that suits their profile. With no genuine pace pressure and a field full of hold-up horses unable to launch from deep, the leader conserves energy and wins comfortably without being headed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Hold-Up Horses Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group collectively push the pace into a genuinely strong gallop and the race develops into an end-to-end test that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: A hot pace drains the front-runners through the final mile, opening a gap for the best of the true closers to slide through — Jouster, who has consistent form at this trip and genuinely stays, and The Dara Man, an 11-year-old with solid course form, are best equipped to finish off if given the gaps. However, this scenario is materially less likely given so many nominal hold-up horses are not true closers and the race shape is unlikely to produce the honest gallop they need.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test, Attrition Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the Going proves testing beneath the unknown going description and the extended trip becomes a stamina slog that culls the field through jumping errors.
scenarios.body: A war of attrition at 2m7f on a potentially demanding surface favours proven stayers with sound jumping records — Kilashee has won at this trip, and Fr Gilligansvoyge has relentless placed form at similar distances. Errors and tired jumping late would eliminate most of the hold-up brigade before the straight, leaving only the cleanest jumpers still on their feet.

watchPoints.text: Tippin And Tappin's jumping must be monitored closely — if they make a significant error at any point in the first mile, the controlled pace scenario collapses and the race shape changes fundamentally, opening the door for prominent pursuers like Following Orders or Lecale's Diamond to capitalise immediately.

Early Arrival has not raced in 329 days and is an 11-year-old chaser — watch in the parade ring and first few fences for any signs of ring rust or jumping hesitancy that would end its race long before the stamina test begins.

The five runners carrying reserve jockey tags (Ladies Well, Mobile Mamma, Johnny M) could see late jockey changes that materially alter tactics — particularly Ladies Well, whose rider could change the front-running intent entirely.

Three County Star, Annie Questions and Johnny M are all flagged as horses that fade in finishes at this sort of trip — if any of them jump to the front or secure a prominent position early against their nature, they could set a false pace that collapses dramatically in the straight and distorts the race shape.

Love Like This ran only 7 days ago and is trained by John Patrick Ryan, who also saddles The Dara Man and Kilashee — watch for any yard-level positional tactics between these three runners that could influence how aggressively Love Like This is ridden from the front.

races.name: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Steeplechase (Div II)

runners_data.name: The Rebel County
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with six-year-old athleticism; Alan O'Sullivan (5) claims, trainer 0/6 in the last 14 days, but solid sim-going record of 11/15 over good; needs a strong pace to deliver from off it and this race may not provide that.|

runners_data.name: Huntsgrove
runners_data.note: Brian Barry (7) takes the ride on this hold-up type who has a strong sim-going record (13/15 on good) and placed form at this trip; 49 days off is manageable for an eight-year-old, though the style puts him at the mercy of how genuinely the race is run.|

runners_data.name: Temptationinmilan
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up specialist whose last six runs show no win and no place on good ground despite facing similar company; the 57-day break and amateur jockey compound the concern, and the form string P450-7 is not encouraging.|

runners_data.name: Kilkee Bay
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and ran well enough last time to suggest the bounce-back 1/22f/SOF form is genuine; a prominent runner whose 39-day freshness and E McNamara training angle give him each-way claims if he stays out of trouble in an 18-runner field.|

runners_data.name: Stretchemout
runners_data.note: Won over 21f on good ground and has placed twice at bigger trips; tongue-strap and hood combination suggests a horse who needs settling, and the hold-up tag means Darragh O'Keeffe will have to nurse him into contention from off a pace that may not be severe enough.|

runners_data.name: Parkgarve
runners_data.note: Consistently prominent but yet to win on good ground in five attempts shown; the tongue-strap is on, PJ O'Hanlon rides, and the trainer has sent out 0/12 in 14 days — takes plenty of winning from this record.|

runners_data.name: Schiehallion
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with genuine placed form at 24f on good ground (2/24f/GOO) and the sim-going record backs it up at 13/15; wears a hood and Alix Balfe (7) claims, but the course profile and placed form here make him one to watch if he travels prominently.|

runners_data.name: My Cullen
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has struggled badly in recent outings (60-F90), with no placed run shown in sim-going for good ground; hood fitted, Harry Sexton (7) up for trainer Hanlon who is 0/27 in the last 14 days — hard to make a case.|

runners_data.name: Ferdia
runners_data.note: Shows natural hold-up tendencies across his last five runs but, with the rear of this field genuinely overcrowded, Daniel King may find him racing further forward than ideal; ten-year-old whose last five have all been outside the places on both good and heavy.|

runners_data.name: Oogum Boogum
runners_data.note: Has won twice at 24f on good going and placed four more times; a consistent prominent performer for Budds with a strong sim-going record (12/15), and the 3P-132 form string is the most competitive in this field — this horse suits the likely race shape closely.|

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a tongue-strap; has placed on good ground at this sort of trip and Joshua Halford (7) claims, but the P3-7P0 recent form and 80 OR limit the optimism despite a healthy sim-going record of 14/15.|

runners_data.name: Three Tribes
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer who is now nine and carries a fades-in-finish warning; redistributed to midfield because of overcrowding at the rear, and the style fit of 0.90 confirms this horse is unlikely to get the ground he truly needs — form includes a P last time.|

runners_data.name: Cullenwaine
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has placed three times at 22f on good ground (2-2-4 in recent handicap chases); Shane O'Callaghan (3) claims three pounds and the 143lb weight is competitive — the blinkered headgear and consistent placed form make this horse interesting in a race that suits front-to-midfield types.|

runners_data.name: Robin Elite
runners_data.note: The redistribution note here is telling — a natural hold-up horse whose form reads 0PP-0P and who carries a fades-in-finish flag; Kevin Murphy (7) has limited material to work with and the 61-day absence adds risk.|

runners_data.name: The Border Boy
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old whose true style is prominent but who is mapped to midfield because prominent slots are genuinely contested; the sim-going record is 15/15 on good ground which is exceptional consistency, though the 638-04 form at this OR suggests he has not been threatening lately.|

runners_data.name: Embrace The Day
runners_data.note: The key pace figure in this race — a young five-year-old who won at 24f on good going and is likely to control the tempo under Keith Donoghue for Gavin Cromwell (strong 14-day strike rate at 1/45); the fade-in-finish flag and style-fit discount are the main risks, but positional control counts for a great deal at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Watty Show
runners_data.note: De Bromhead has had a productive 14 days (5/35); however, this six-year-old's natural position is hold-up and, with the rear overcrowded, he is effectively displaced from his ideal role — recent form of 7P0-78 and a fades-in-finish flag combine to undermine confidence.|

runners_data.name: Amburana
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose hold-up style puts him in the same overcrowded rear cluster as Watty Show and Three Tribes; the fade-in-finish flag, style fit of 0.92, and uninspired 043-70 form on surfaces where he has managed just one placed run in nine sim-going races make this very difficult to recommend.|

races.paceDynamic: Embrace The Day is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Kilkee Bay, Parkgarve, Schiehallion, Oogum Boogum, and U Asking Me as genuine prominent types to challenge, is likely to get a largely uncontested lead over 2m7f on good ground at Killarney. The pace will be sustainable rather than scorching — Embrace The Day carries a fade-in-finish flag, so the question is whether that lead is enough to hold off closers who track within range throughout. This field holds considerably more prominent and hold-up types than the race map can accommodate; The Border Boy, Ferdia, Watty Show, Amburana, and Three Tribes are true hold-up or prominent horses redistributed to midfield because the rear of the field is genuinely overcrowded with closers who cannot all get their natural position. The tactical verdict favours horses tracking in second or third place with enough stamina to reel in Embrace The Day — prominent-to-midfield stalkers who travel within two or three lengths of the lead and pick up after the last fence are best placed, with true deep hold-up types unlikely to get the ground they need in a race that will not be run at a truly searching gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Embrace The Day Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Embrace The Day bowls along at a comfortable clip and the prominent pack fail to apply sustained pressure through the final mile.
scenarios.body: Embrace The Day dictates from the front at a measured gallop, giving prominent trackers like Kilkee Bay and Oogum Boogum every chance to stay close, but the fade-in-finish concern is mitigated by the lack of pressure; horses who travel prominently in the first three or four positions throughout and jump fluently are handed a decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to stretch Embrace The Day from the back straight and the first or second in the market lands a telling blow between the last two fences.
scenarios.body: Oogum Boogum, Cullenwaine, and Schiehallion, all genuine prominent types who can travel in the slipstream of the leader, are ideally placed to pounce as Embrace The Day fades; the 2m7f trip on good ground rewards horses who have been positive throughout and carry stamina in their profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stayers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final mile and the race turns into a slog, allowing horses dropped in mid-division to stay competitive.
scenarios.body: The Rebel County and Huntsgrove, both genuine hold-up types with course-and-distance profiles on good ground, could creep into contention if the field concertinas approaching the final three fences; this scenario is mildly discounted because several horses mapped to midfield are redistributed types rather than true closers, which reduces the probability of a well-timed late swoop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Thins The Field
scenarios.trigger: If a high-fall or jumping incident at a key fence disrupts the race order and produces a truly contested or compressed finish.
scenarios.body: An 18-runner handicap chase on good ground raises the statistical risk of interference and fallers, which could compress the field and bring unconsidered hold-up types into play; Stretchemout, who has shown form over similar trips and going, could benefit from a chaotic finish, while the overcrowded midfield creates collision risk at the open ditches.

watchPoints.text: Embrace The Day's fade-in-finish flag is the central danger point — watch whether Keith Donoghue sets an overly leisurely gallop that allows the prominent pack to cruise within striking distance and overhaul him before the last.|

With 18 runners in a 2m7f handicap chase, the first two or three fences are high-risk for pile-ups; any incident involving the tightly-bunched midfield group could eliminate several of the redistributed hold-up types (Watty Show, Ferdia, Three Tribes) simultaneously.|

Oogum Boogum's tongue-strap and consistent prominent profile make him the horse most likely to expose Embrace The Day if the pace slackens — watch whether Shane Fitzgerald sends him forward to take a position close to the lead early.|

Cullenwaine's form of 2-2-4 in recent handicap chases suggests a horse creeping up the handicap; Shane O'Callaghan's 3lb claim effectively brings him in near the top of the competitive range, and his headgear change to blinkered is worth noting if he travels prominently.|

The Border Boy's exceptional sim-going record of 15/15 on good ground is a standout statistic, but Phillip Enright will need to manoeuvre from a position further back than natural — watch the early stages to see whether he can recover enough ground to factor.|

races.name: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) Flat Race
